title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Starting point
AI system and date: ChatGPT, November 4, 2026.
Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address.
Our research question is how the use of AI is associated with students’ performance on an unassisted math test, holding previous GPA and grade level constant. There are three levels of AI use, including the control, GPT Base, and GPT Tutor. We use Session 1 data from non-honor classes. Our baseline model is a multiple linear regression model: Part3Tot ~ Treatment arm + gpa_prev + Year.
Our baseline model estimate that for students with the same previous GPA and grade level, students in the GPT Tutor group score an average of 5.24% higher on an unassisted math test than students in the control group (p=0.0077), and students in the GPT Base group score an average of 0.55% lower on an unassisted math test than students in the control group (p=0.789). The baseline model explains about 31.9% of the variation in exam score.
A limitation is that the baseline model assumes that the group effect of AI use is the same across the range of previous GPA and grade level in our sample. However, our box plots suggest that the group effect of AI use may differ for different grade levels. We want to use an extension to address this limitation.

text:
My decisions

Accepted: We accepted the advice of using random forest to capture nonlinear relationship and possible interactions that may not be considered in the baseline model.
Changed: We adjusted AI’s suggestion and plan to compare the random forest model with the baseline model using the same response and explanation variable. We will also compare their predictive ability using the same cross-validation folds and keep the regression model as our main tool.
Rejected or corrected: We have not identified an error in the AI response yet. We are not going to plot the group differences as suggested by AI until we better understand how to interpret it.

Connection to the final case study: Identify where the extension’s method and result appear on the final page and how they strengthen the course-based analysis.
The extension’s method will appear in the “A new direction with AI” section in the final report. We will show the result of the extension method and our independent checks. We will briefly explain the method and presenting a table comparing the cross-validated RMSE of the random forest model and that of the course-based model. The random forest allows us to have a more flexible model. Comparing their cross-validated RMSE allows us to assess whether a random forest model is needed. If there is a big improvement in the cross-validated RMSE of the random forest model, it can suggest that we missed nonlinear relationship or interaction in our baseline model.

title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Independent verification

Check and result: We will check the code written by AI using the official document for the R package randomForest. Specifically, we will verify how random forest regressions generate predictions and what each parameter is doing in the code. We will compare the AI-generated code with the document. Link to the document: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/randomForest/randomForest.pdf. This is a planned comparison and has not been completed yet.
Check and result: Rather than blindly trusting the AI output, we will copy all AI code and run it ourselves in R-studio and/ or positron. This will allow us to verify that the AI code is accurate and runs how we want it to, as well as verify that the expected output of the AI code is accurate. We will also compare the cross-validated RMSE of the random forest regression model with that of our baseline model. If the random forest regression model had a significantly smaller cross-validated RMSE, we could know that there are some elements that the baseline model fail to capture. If there was not a big difference in the cross-validated RMSE, then we could know that a more complicated model is not necessary.

Link or cite verification sources where appropriate. A second AI response does not count as independent verification.

title: AI Use and Verification
text:
Remaining limitation
Even if the random forest regression model predicts new data better than the baseline model, there is still some limitations. An obvious limitation is that a random forest regression model is harder to interpret than a regression model. The random forest does not provide coefficients that describe the change in response when one predictor changes after accounting for other predictors. A random forest also does not test the significance of coefficients. We will still use regression as our main tool, but we will add some nonlinear terms and interaction terms to our regression model.
